title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: $\tilde X^{*an}$ is a finite covering of $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, i.e. a dessin d'enfant. Its barycentric-type triangulation has triangles (flags) $r$ in a set $Q$ (called $R$ on the previous page). Three involutions $\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\sigma_\infty$ act on $Q$; $\sigma_i$ reflects a triangle across the side opposite vertex $i$. The punctures $R_s$ are indexed by $s\in S=S_0\sqcup S_1\sqcup S_\infty$, the vertices of types $0,1,\infty$.

Goal: list many presentations of the fundamental groupoid by generators and relations, using different sets of base points near sides or vertices. On the previous pages Grothendieck had $1+3$ presentations and then $3$ more. Here he gives the last family of three, so $10=1+3+3+3$ cases.

The case worked out here keeps only base points of type $0$-$1$ ("type 0" in his wording):
- **Base points (20).** $R_r^{0,1}$, $r\in Q$, with $R_r^{0,1}=R^{0,1}_{\sigma_\infty r}$. So the base points are in bijection with $Q/\sigma_\infty$, i.e. the edges of the dessin.
- **Generators (21).**
  - $\Lambda^0_r: R^{0,1}_r\to R^{0,1}_{\sigma_1 r}$ turns around the type-0 vertex, crossing the side $0\infty$.
  - $A^{0,1}_r := (a^\infty_{\sigma_0 r})^{-1}\Lambda'^1_r a^\infty_r : R^{0,1}_r\to R^{0,1}_{\sigma_0 r}$ turns around the type-1 vertex. It is obtained from the earlier presentation (17)-(19) by eliminating the intermediate base points $R^{1,0}$. The composite type-checks: $a^\infty_r: R^{01}_r\to R^{10}_r$, then $\Lambda'^1_r: R^{10}_r\to R^{10}_{\sigma_0 r}$, then $(a^\infty_{\sigma_0 r})^{-1}$.
- **Relations (22).** Only the redundancy relations $\Lambda^0_r\Lambda^0_{\sigma_1 r}=1$ and $A^{0,1}_rA^{0,1}_{\sigma_0 r}=1$. They express that the generator attached to the flag $r$ and the one attached to the mirror flag are mutually inverse.

Conclusion: $\Pi_1(\tilde X^{*an},\{R^{0,1}_r\})$ is the free groupoid on one 'rotation around 0' and one 'rotation around 1' per edge. This is the standard description of the fiber over a point of $]0,1[$ as a set with two permutations: the monodromy of the free group $\langle\gamma_0,\gamma_1\rangle$.

"Bouchage des trous": to pass to the compactified curve, one adds for each $s\in S$ one relation saying that the local loop around $R_s$ is trivial. The next page continues: "exprimer que ce lacet local est $\simeq 1$". Grothendieck calls this essentially trivial in all cases.
errors: No mathematical error. Euler characteristic check: $|E|$ vertices and $2|E|$ free generators give $\chi=-|E|=d\cdot\chi(\mathbb P^1\setminus 3\text{ pts})$, as it should.
Notation drifts: $\tau_i$ and $R$ on the previous page become $\sigma_i$ and $Q$ here.
The arrow in (21) should be $\Lambda'^1_r$, as defined in (18) on the previous page.
The ordering convention of the composites is functional (right to left) and is left implicit.

ideas.what: Presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a dessin (a covering of $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$), with base points on the edges, as a free groupoid generated by rotations around black and white vertices.
ideas.modern_name: Dessins d'enfants / permutation-pair (monodromy) description; covering groupoid of the free group $F_2$
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); classical Riemann existence theorem / Hurwitz; Jones–Singerman (1978) for maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, groupoids with several base points), in spirit; not this explicit list

ideas.what: Systematic enumeration ($10=1+3+3+3$) of presentations according to which base points (near which vertex types) are retained, eliminating the others.
ideas.modern_name: Change of base-point set in presentations of fundamental groupoids (Tietze moves for groupoids)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (groupoids with many base points), Higgins

ideas.what: 'Bouchage des trous': obtaining $\pi_1$ of the compactified surface by adding one local-loop relation per puncture.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine bookkeeping of presentations of the fundamental groupoid of a dessin, varying the choice of base points. The mathematics is standard, and the approach is consistent with the Esquisse's emphasis on many-base-point groupoids.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'Je vais donner trois autres présentations, où on éliminerait non seulement les V^ts proches (disons) des R_s sommets de type ∞ [et les sommets placés dans les lois dérivées?], mais aussi ceux proches des sommets (disons) de type 1, en ne gardant donc que les sommets R_r^{0,1} de type 0'. The text reads 'éliminerait', not 's'écarterait', and 'en ne gardant donc que', not 'en prenant donc pour'. The interlinear insertion is 'trois' (≈ 'tions'), consistent with 10=1+3+3+3, rather than 'tous'.
In (21) the middle factor appears to be $\Lambda'^1_r$ (with prime), as in (18) of the previous page.
The fundamental groupoid is $\Pi_1(\tilde X^{*an},\{R^{0,1}_r\}_{r\in Q})$; the space is $\tilde X^{*an}$.

'Dans ce fait des façons essentiellement triviales' is probably 'Dans chacun des quatre cas, il suffit/on trouve des flèches génératrices diverses, définies...'; the 'se fait de façon essentiellement triviale' clause is part of the preceding sentence.
